allowed_dependency_manifest.content: Let n, k, l ∈ Z with 0 ≤ k, l ≤ n. Define R(q) = [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q in the natural rational-function setting for Gaussian q-binomial coefficients. If R(q) lies in a polynomial ring in q (i.e., R(q) has only finitely many nonnegative powers of q with coefficients in the relevant coefficient ring), then when written as R(q) = Σ_i c_i q^i, every coefficient c_i satisfies c_i ≥ 0.

forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, l with 0 ≤ k, l ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q is a polynomial in q, then that polynomial has only nonnegative coefficients.

payload.role_in_assembly: This is the new core structural input: it replaces the prior cyclotomic-positivity bottleneck by a weighted complete-intersection realization theorem.

domain_restrictions: R(q) must be well-defined as a formal expression: [n choose l]_q ≠ 0 and division is interpreted in the ambient field/ring where Gaussian coefficients live (typically Q(q) or a localization of Z[q])
the premise “is a polynomial in q” means R(q) has no negative powers of q (i.e., R(q) ∈ coefficient_ring[q] for some coefficient ring)

domain_restrictions: A,B,d are integers with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0
Empty product convention: if d=0 then ∏_{i=1}^0 (...) = 1 so Q_{A,B,0}(q)=1
Assumption: the rational expression Q_{A,B,d}(q) is actually a polynomial, i.e., Q_{A,B,d}(q) ∈ Q[q] (not just a rational function)
Graded ring S is Q[x_1,...,x_d] with weighted grading deg(x_i)=B+i for i=1..d
If d=0, interpret S as Q (no variables, hence no f_i witnesses needed)
Each f_i is homogeneous in S with weighted degree deg(f_i)=A+i
Regularity condition: in the successive quotient S/(f_1,...,f_{i-1}), the class of f_i is not a zero-divisor (equivalently: (f_1,...,f_d) is a homogeneous regular sequence in S)
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Let A,B,d ∈ Z with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0, and define Q_{A,B,d}(q)=∏_{i=1}^d (1-q^{A+i})/(1-q^{B+i}) with Q_{A,B,0}(q)=1. If Q_{A,B,d}(q) ∈ Q[q], then in the weighted graded polynomial ring S=Q[x_1,...,x_d] (or S=Q if d=0) with deg(x_i)=B+i, there exist homogeneous elements f_1,...,f_d ∈ S such that deg(f_i)=A+i for each i=1..d and for each i the class of f_i in S/(f_1,...,f_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor (so f_1,...,f_d form a homogeneous regular sequence). Consequently, the graded data of S modulo this regular sequence yields the given expression Q_{A,B,d}(q) (as stated in the equivalence).

payload.statement_nl: For integers A, B, d with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0, define Q_{A,B,d}(q) := prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(A+i)) / (1 - q^(B+i)), with the empty product equal to 1 when d = 0. Assume Q_{A,B,d}(q) belongs to Q[q]. Let S be the weighted polynomial ring Q[x_1, ..., x_d] graded by deg(x_i) = B+i; when d = 0 interpret S as Q. Then there exist homogeneous polynomials f_1, ..., f_d in S such that deg(f_i) = A+i for every i, and for each i the image of f_i in S/(f_1, ..., f_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor. Equivalently, Q_{A,B,d}(q) is realized by a homogeneous regular sequence in a weighted polynomial ring with variable weights B+1, ..., B+d and relation degrees A+1, ..., A+d.
